content:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a 12-18% drop in prefix-cache hit rate on prod after yday's attn-kernel-v2 + q8 rollout. 95th tail latency +40ms on chat routes. :eyes:

deploy-bot: attn-kernel-v2 rolled to prod (fleet alpha,beta,gamma) at 2026-03-15T22:08Z (rollout id: r-20260315-22-attn-v2).

sanjay: link to dashboard? can you pull the per-model hit rate vs time?

maya: https://internal.grafana/redwood/runtime/prefix-cache?from=2026-03-14&to=2026-03-16 — baseline (before) ~0.62 overall, post-rollout ~0.51. quick snapshot: baseline 62.3% -> 49.8% after kernel switch on alpha/beta.

olivia: I ran a profile on a failing request and dumped the cache key serialization. weirdly the serialized prefix fingerprint includes a kernel variant tag now: `kv_meta.build_id:attn-v2` for some requests. That would make cached entries not match older keys. snippet: ```kv_key = sha1(prompt_bytes + kv_meta.version + kv_meta.build_id)```

leo: hmm — runtime shouldn't be injecting build_id into the canonical key. expected behavior is build-agnostic keying so warmups are shared across kernels. any recent change to keying logic/serializers?

ashley: I grep'd the change log — there was a small normalization change in the compiled kernel wrapper that added a `runtime_metadata` blob to the kv object to help debugging. It looks like serialization landed in prod when the wrapper started returning kv objects upstream.

maya: Confirmed: warmup jobs write keys without build_id, but new requests are including it, so warmups can't populate the same entries -> hit-rate drop. Also saw some requests have padding bytes in prompt serialization depending on vectorized-attn path, so key diffs are multi-factor.

sanjay: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback attn-kernel-v2 on fleets with high cache dependency, 2) deploy a hotfix to strip runtime_metadata from key before hashing, 3) run backfill warmup that computes both old and new key variants. Which do we want?

leo: Rollback for alpha & beta immediately for safety. Apply hotfix to prod canary to validate strip logic. Backfill should be lower priority because it costs tokens/compute.

maya: +1 rollback alpha/beta. creating an incident and will assign owner. cc @runtime-qa-bot for tests.

runtime-qa-bot: Incident created — INC-2026-1325: "prefix-cache keying regression after attn-kernel-v2". Severity: P2. Assignees: maya, leo, olivia. Runbook checklist attached.

olivia: Patch draft for hotfix (python-ish pseudo): ```# on key generation path
kv_meta = kv_meta if kv_meta else {}
kv_meta.pop('build_id', None)
serialized = serialize_prefix(prompt, kv_meta)
key = sha1(serialized)``` Will open PR against runtime-keys branch after rollback is in progress. Need a quick unit test that simulates both padded and unpadded serializations.

ashley: Also adding normalization step to collapse repeated whitespace and canonicalize newline endings — that should reduce diffs caused by tokenizer variant between kernels.

maya: Action items: leo rollback alpha/beta (in flight), olivia open PR + canary deploy hotfix, sanjay monitor grafana -> report hit-rate and p50/p95 after rollback. I'll coordinate a warmup backfill plan if hotfix doesn't recover 95% of the lost hits.

leo: rollback started on alpha at 22:28Z. will confirm when complete.

maya: alpha rollback done. partial recovery seen on alpha (hit-rate +7% so far). will wait for beta.

san jay: (typo) — sanjay: beta rollback done at 22:36Z, observing +9% on that fleet. still ~3-4% lower than pre-rollout overall because gamma still on v2.

olivia: opened PR #4892 with key-strip hotfix + tests. will run canary on gamma next.

maya: good progress — if canary recovers we can continue progressive rollout with hotfix. if not, full rollback. keeping this thread as source of truth.

leo: final note — we should add a linter check to prevent runtime_metadata fields from being included in key material in future. filing infra task. :+1:"
